title: Radiology's Last Exam (RadLE)
problemStatement: Can AI read a chest X-ray as well as a radiologist?
summary: A landmark benchmark testing frontier multimodal AI against board-certified radiologists on complex, multi-finding radiology cases.

children.text: RadLE was built to answer a blunt question that most healthcare AI vendors avoid: how far are current frontier models from expert clinical performance when the cases are messy, ambiguous, and real?
The benchmark compares expert radiologists, trainees, and multimodal AI models on chest radiology tasks that require clinical reasoning rather than pattern matching alone.
Its headline result matters beyond rankings: the best AI crossed trainee-level performance, but still remained far behind experts, defining a clearer threshold for responsible deployment.

title: Autonomous Radiology Report Generation
problemStatement: Can AI autonomously write radiology reports that radiologists trust?
summary: Multidimensional evaluation framework for autonomous optimization pipelines in personalized head CT and chest radiograph report generation.

children.text: This work studies how autonomous report-writing systems should be judged when correctness, clarity, uncertainty calibration, and workflow fit all matter at once.

title: National Healthcare Data Commons
problemStatement: What does responsible healthcare data infrastructure look like at national scale?
summary: Building federated, privacy-preserving platforms for secure healthcare data sharing — addressing India's clinical data fragmentation.

children.text: The Data Commons program explores how to make clinical data more usable for science without compromising privacy, governance, or institutional autonomy.

title: India-Specific Clinical AI Validation
problemStatement: Why do AI diagnostics fail in Indian clinical contexts?
summary: Systematic evaluation of how frontier AI models perform on clinical data from Indian healthcare settings versus the Western datasets they were trained on.

children.text: Many medical AI systems inherit assumptions from the datasets, hardware, reporting styles, and patient populations they were trained on. This program measures the resulting gap in Indian hospitals.

heroImage.alt: Clinical validation dashboard for Indian healthcare contexts

title: Human-Centric Radiology AI Design
problemStatement: How do we build AI systems that clinicians actually trust?
summary: Co-creating intuitive AI tools with frontline clinicians. Hyper-personalized documentation systems and trusted AI-driven assistants.

children.text: Clinical adoption is not a model score problem alone. This work studies interface design, workflow integration, and clinician oversight patterns that make AI usable in practice.

heroImage.alt: Clinician working with an AI-assisted radiology interface

title: Governance and Ethics of Medical AI
problemStatement: Who is responsible when AI misdiagnoses a patient?
summary: Building evaluation and governance frameworks for clinical AI that go beyond accuracy — addressing fairness, explainability, and accountability.

children.text: CRASH Lab treats governance as a design problem, not a compliance afterthought. The goal is to define what responsible clinical AI deployment should require before systems scale.
